sections.h2: What does the Bay County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Bay County Register of Deeds is the county's record keeper for land. It accepts deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices, certified copies and other instruments, indexes them, and keeps the public record that title companies search before a Bay County sale closes.

The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Research hours inside the office run from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and stay open through lunch. Since January 1, 2018 the office has numbered documents with a single Document Number, and it no longer uses Liber and Page.

  • Online searching runs around the clock through Doxpop, with a help line of 1-866-369-7671 for sign-up problems.
  • Doxpop Property Watch is a free alert that emails you if someone tries to transfer your land title.
  • eRecording is offered through approved partners listed on the office page.
  • Mailed documents sent by USPS, UPS or FedEx need a self-addressed stamped return envelope.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Bay County?
sections.html:
The county's statutory fee page lists a flat $30.00 for each document, whether it is a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or other instrument. Of that, $4.00 goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund. The $4.00 is not charged on fixture filings, state or federal liens, state deeds, plats or tax reversion documents.

Bay County recording charges. Source: Bay County Register of Deeds fee page.
ItemCharge
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30.00 flat per document
Document that assigns or discharges several instruments$3.00 for each added instrument
Tax certificate (separate check to the Bay County Treasurer)$5.00
UCC financing statement or fixture filing$30.00
State transfer tax$7.50 per $1,000 of consideration
County transfer tax$1.10 per $1,000 of consideration

The tax certificate applies to warranty deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contract with a warranty clause, and condominium master deeds, as required by MCL 211.135.

sections.h2: What does a document need before Bay County will record it?
sections.html:
The office publishes a sixteen point checklist drawn from Michigan recording law. Documents that miss a point get returned, which can delay a closing by days. These are the items that trip up sellers most often.

  • Signatures must be original, with each name typed or printed beneath it, and the names must match the notary block.
  • The deed needs the grantee's street or post office address, plus the name and address of whoever drafted it.
  • An acknowledgment by a Michigan notary, judge or court clerk is required on documents conveying or encumbering land.
  • The first page needs a margin of at least 2.5 inches at the top and half an inch on the other sides, with black type of at least 10 point on white paper.
  • Paper size must fall between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches, and the first line must state what the instrument is.
  • If a deed names a surviving owner, a certified death certificate must be recorded with it or already of record.
  • Court orders must carry the clerk's certification and seal, and the first five digits of any Social Security number must be removed.

Michigan also expects the marital status of male grantors on conveyances, under the statute the office cites as MCLA 565.221.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a Bay County sale?
sections.html:
Two taxes apply at recording: the county tax under MCL 207.505 and the state tax under MCL 207.526. The deed has to state the full consideration on its face, or a Real Estate Transfer Affidavit disclosing it must be handed in with the instrument. Each tax is collected unless the transfer is exempt, and the exemption has to be written on the face of the document.

Take a sale at the Census median value for Bay County of $152,200. At $7.50 per thousand the state share comes to about $1,141, and at $1.10 per thousand the county share is about $167. Roughly $1,309 changes hands as tax at recording.

The exemption lists differ. Both acts exempt instruments with consideration under $100, mortgage security instruments, leases, court orders without stated consideration, land contracts where title has not passed, and transfers given in foreclosure of government backed loans. The state act adds conveyances from a person to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, which the county act's exemption list leaves out. Ask the title agent or the office which exemption fits your deed.

sections.h2: What state fee rules sit behind the Bay County schedule?
sections.html:
Michigan's Revised Judicature Act, MCL 600.2567, sets what a register of deeds may charge, and the Bay County page cites it. Beyond the $30 recording fee, the statute lists charges for the services sellers and heirs ask for most.

  • Copies of records are $1.00 per page, and certifying a recorded document is $5.00.
  • A records search by grantor and grantee costs 50 cents per year searched, with a $5.00 minimum.
  • Filing any other paper and making an entry costs $1.00.
  • Payment is due when the document is left for recording, with exceptions for electronic filings and for government filers on a payment schedule.

The statute lets a charter county set a different schedule by ordinance, so confirm any copy or search charge with the Bay County office before you mail a check.

sections.h2: In what order should a Bay County seller handle recording?
sections.html:
A clean sequence saves a trip. First, confirm who signs and whether the deed names a survivor, so the death certificate is ready. Second, request the tax certificate from the County Treasurer if the deed carries a warranty. Third, have the deed drafted with the full consideration stated, or prepare the transfer affidavit. Fourth, notarize in Michigan and hand the original to the title agent or mail it with a return envelope.

After recording, the office assigns a Document Number rather than a Liber and Page. Keep that number for your own file, since it is how the instrument is found in the online index. Consider signing up for Property Watch once the sale closes if you keep other land in the county.

If a document comes back unrecorded, the cause is usually on the sixteen point checklist: a mismatched name, a thin margin, an unsealed court order or an unredacted Social Security number. Fix the single defect and resubmit rather than redrafting the whole instrument.

sections.h2: Where does the Register of Deeds fit with other Bay County offices?
sections.html:
A sale touches more than one office. The Treasurer, on the sixth floor of the Bay County Building at 515 Center Ave., issues the tax certificate and collects delinquent tax. The Equalization Department answers parcel and description questions. Each city and township assessor holds the value record, and the Register keeps the chain of title.

Bay County sits on Saginaw Bay on the east side of Michigan's lower peninsula and has 14 townships and 4 cities. Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows a median owner occupied home value of $152,200, 77.0 percent owner occupancy, 45,103 households and median household income of $61,763. Home building is slow, with 67 permits counted for 2025.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Bay County?
faqs.a: It is a flat $30.00 per document, with $4.00 of that sent to the State Survey and Remonumentation fund. Assignments or discharges covering more than one instrument add $3.00 for each extra one.

faqs.q: Can I search Bay County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. Doxpop provides online searching all day, every day, and the office suggests its free Property Watch alert so you hear about any attempt to transfer your title.
Yes. The office lists approved eRecording partners on its page for delivering title documents online.

faqs.q: How much is the tax certificate for a warranty deed?
faqs.a: It is $5.00, paid with a separate check made out to the Bay County Treasurer, not the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: What are the transfer tax rates in Bay County?
faqs.a: The Register lists $7.50 per $1,000 of consideration for the state and $1.10 per $1,000 for the county. Exempt transfers must say so on the instrument.
